We need to produce a completed test class for Position.getGrossReturn(Num entryPrice, Num exitPrice). Need to set up Position with entry trade and maybe exit trade? The method uses getEntry().isBuy() to decide. So we need a Position where entry is BUY and another where entry is SELL. Use constructors: new Position(entry, exit, ...) or use Position(TradeType) then operate to create entry and exit? Simpler: create Trade objects directly via static methods Trade.buyAt etc. In existing tests they use Trade.buyAt(index, price, amount, transactionModel). For our test we don't need cost models maybe default zero cost. Use Trade.buyAt(0, DoubleNum.valueOf(10), DoubleNum.valueOf(1)) etc.

We then create Position using new Position(entry, exit) which uses entry.getCostModel() and zero holding cost. Need transaction cost model maybe default zero.

Test cases:

1. When entry is BUY, gross return = exitPrice / entryPrice.

2. When entry is SELL, gross return = exitPrice / entryPrice - 1, then negate, then +1 => formula: 1 - (exit/entry -1) = 2 - exit/entry? Wait compute: exit/entry => ratio. minus one => ratio-1. negate => -(ratio-1) = 1 - ratio. plus one => (1 - ratio) + 1 = 2 - ratio. So gross return = 2 - (exit/entry). Let's verify with example: entry 10, exit 5 (short). Expected gross return? For short, profit = (entry - exit)/entry = 0.5, gross return maybe 1 + profit? Not sure. We'll just test using method's logic.

We'll compute expected using Num operations: entryPrice = DoubleNum.valueOf(10); exitPrice = DoubleNum.valueOf(5); expected = exitPrice.dividedBy(entryPrice).minus(entryPrice.numOf(1)).negate().plus(entryPrice.numOf(1));

But entryPrice.numOf(1) returns Num representing 1 using same type; we can use DoubleNum.valueOf(1).

Test both.

Also test with NaN? Not needed.
